messages:
maria: heads up — after the toolkit-12 image rollout to eu-west canary, a few nodes are failing container startup with `modprobe: ERROR: could not insert 'nvidia_uvm': Exec format error` and then OOM eviction on the kubelet side.
ajay: which image tag? we pushed `redwood/toolkit:12.0.1-gcc13` last night.
maria: that one. stacktrace from kubelet logs:
```
Mar 15 08:12:02 node-42 kubelet[1290]: containerd: starting container
Mar 15 08:12:02 node-42 kernel: nvidia_uvm: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing - tainting kernel
Mar 15 08:12:02 node-42 kernel: nvidia_uvm: Exec format error
Mar 15 08:12:03 node-42 kubelet: Pod sandbox changed, restarting container
Mar 15 08:12:09 node-42 kubelet: eviction: imagefs.available < threshold
```
olivia: looks like the compiled kernel module in the image doesn't match the host kernel (we're on 5.15.0-88) — likely GCC/ABI mismatch from the toolchain rebuild.
ajay: we switched to gcc-13 for the cu12 builds to avoid PTX issues, but didn't run `dkms` or build modules against the host kernel.
maria: right — the modules included are prebuilt for 5.19 and fail to load, then fallback tries to use a user-space shim that allocs lots of memory and triggers eviction.
tim: impact: ~6 canary nodes in eu-west flapped, ~20 pods evicted; GPU capacity dropped ~15% for that AZ. any service outages?
maria: no customer-facing errors yet, but batch workloads time out and internal infra tests failed. noticed NCCL errors when containers did start: `NCCL WARN Call to cudaGetDevice failed : CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN`.
ajay: immediate mitigation: rolling image back to `toolkit:11.8.0-gcc11` on canary nodes, cordon + drain affected nodes to avoid new scheduling, and add a taint to block gpu-pods on the remaining canaries until we validate kernel modules.
olivia: can we hotfix by mounting host drivers into containers instead of shipping modules? that would avoid mismatch but we lose reproducibility.
tim: short term mount host `/lib/modules` and `/usr/src` into the runtime pod + set `--privileged` for canary only. Also need to update our node-drain hooks to skip heavy batch jobs.
maria: agreed. ajay — can you prepare a rollback image and a CI gate to prevent `gcc13` toolchain image from promoting until we test module compatibility matrix? add kernel versions we support.
ajay: on it. Also adding a presubmit that runs `modinfo` against host kernel inside our canary replica using qemu nodes.
sre-bot: deploy started: rollback-image -> redwood/toolkit:11.8.0-gcc11 @ canary-eu-west (initiated by ajay)
deploy-bot: rollout 10% -> canary-eu-west in progress :hourglass_flowing_sand:
maria: follow-ups: 1) audit all regions for nodes with 5.19+ kernels (we have a few dev boxes), 2) stop auto-promote of gcc13 images until a module build step is added, 3) cost note — extra evictions caused retries and inflated preemptible usage this billing cycle (~$4.5k estimate for eu-west batch retries).
olivia: i'll open infra ticket with kernel/driver matrix and add a checklist for container module builds + DKMS packaging.
ajay: timeline: rollback done in ~6m, then validation run. will post status here.
mar ia: typo in prev msg — rolling forward: status? (typobot)
maria: rollback finished, canaries stable. running validation job against 5.15/5.18/5.19 kernels now. will update ticket.
ajay: re: NCCL warnings — if modules partially load they can leave GPUs in a bad state; we'll add a prestart check that runs `nvidia-smi -L` and exit if it errors to prevent noisy NCCL logs.
tim: thx. once validation passes we need a coordinated window for prod rollout and a rollback playbook (drain+mount-host-modules) documented in incident runbook.
olivia: filing the runbook now, linking to ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-2379 :spiral_notepad:
maria: closing loop — lesson: toolkit upgrades need kernel-module compatibility tests and DKMS packaging before image promotion. :white_check_mark:
